biggest_catch: The $695 annual fee is the story: 125,000 AAdvantage miles after $15,000 in 5 months must clear a $695 fee in year one, and the $15,000 spend requirement ($3,000/month) only makes sense with large already-planned purchases — plus the bonus is a 'limited time offer' that can be pulled from the page.
catches: Claim the bonus only with spending you already planned; never manufacture $15,000 of spend just for the bonus.
The $695 annual fee reduces the bonus — first-year net math is in the biggest catch above. (Fee was $595 until 08/23/2026; new applicants now pay $695.)
Applying for the card causes a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily lower your credit score.
The variable purchase APR is 19.49%–29.49%; carrying a balance on a $15,000 run wipes out the miles value — pay the statement balance in full every month.

Bonus miles are not available if you received a new account bonus for a Citi/AAdvantage Executive account in the past 48 months, or converted another Citi card on which you earned a bonus in the last 48 months into one.
Miles typically appear in your AAdvantage account 8–10 weeks after you meet the spend — keep the account open until they land.

steps: Go to the official Citi page https://www.citi.com/credit-cards/travel-reward-credit-cards?afc=106 and read the Executive bonus terms (125,000 miles after $15,000 in 5 months; $695 annual fee).
Confirm you have not received an Executive new-account bonus in the past 48 months (and have not converted a bonus-earning Citi card into one in the last 48 months).
Apply online through the official Citi page and get approved; save your approval confirmation.
Within the first 5 months, put $15,000 of already-planned purchases on the card — never manufacture spend for the bonus.
Pay the statement balance in full every month — the variable APR is 19.49%–29.49%; carrying a balance destroys the bonus math.
Keep the account open and check your American Airlines AAdvantage account — the 125,000 miles typically appear 8–10 weeks after you meet the spend.
Before the next annual fee bills, decide whether the $695 fee is worth the Admirals Club membership and travel perks, or downgrade.
